tagline: The first coast-to-coast road, through the Iowa towns it left.
intro: Iowa's share of the first transcontinental highway, established in 1913 from Times Square to San Francisco, crosses the state for 503 miles between Council Bluffs and Clinton. Its country takes in the wind-sculpted Loess Hills by the Missouri, the level plains and rolling river valleys of central Iowa, and the steep bluffs of the Mississippi. Farmland is the one constant.

When the road became US 30 and was straightened, most downtowns and several whole towns were bypassed. The old alignment still runs through them, past 1928 Lincoln Highway markers, Burma-Shave signs and canopy gas stations.

moments.title: Ledges State Park
moments.text: South of Boone, Pea's Creek has cut a sandstone gorge up to 100 feet deep, with concretions jutting from the cliffs and stone bridges the CCC built in the 1930s.

moments.title: Reed-Niland Corner, Colo
moments.text: Charlie Reed opened a gas station in 1923 where the Lincoln and Jefferson highways cross, and through the early 1930s it was one of a handful of round-the-clock stops on the Lincoln.

moments.title: Mount Vernon
moments.text: The town's mountain is a paha, a ridge of sand and loess about a mile long and 100 feet high, with uptown at one end and Cornell College at the other.
